        {
          "kind": "recipe_type",

          "source": "file:minecraft/lang-overlays",

        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit.json",
          "text": "Pits of Fire",
          "key": "guide-page:name",
          "label": "Pits of Fire",
          "item_ref_count": 11,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 11
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit.json",
          "text": "Fire is an important technological advancement. In order to create fire, you will need a Firestarter. In order to use, simply hold down on the ground. After a few moments, smoke, and then fire will be created. It may take a couple tries to light successfully.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.0.text",
          "label": "Pits of Fire",
          "item_ref_count": 11,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 11
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit.json",
          "text": "Crafting a firestarter can be done with two sticks.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.1.text",
          "label": "Pits of Fire",
          "item_ref_count": 11,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 11
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit.json",
          "text": "With a firestarter, it is now possible to make a Firepit. In order to make one, you will need one log, three sticks, and optionally up to five pieces of kindling. Kindling can be items such as paper products, straw, or pinecones, and will increase the chance of successfully creating a firepit by 10 percent per item used. Throw () all the items on the ground, on the same block. Then use the firestarter on the block with the items floating above it.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.2.text",
          "label": "Pits of Fire",
          "item_ref_count": 11,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 11
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit.json",
          "text": "If you were successful, a firepit will be created.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.3.text",
          "label": "Pits of Fire",
          "item_ref_count": 11,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 11
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit.json",
          "text": "Using the firepit will now open the firepit screen. On the left are four fuel slots. Logs, Peat, and Stick Bundles can all be used as firepit fuel by placing them in the topmost slot. Fuel will be consumed from the bottommost slot. There is a gauge which displays the current Temperature of the firepit, and on the right, a slot for items to be heated in.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.4.text",
          "label": "Pits of Fire",
          "item_ref_count": 11,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 11
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit.json",
          "text": "The Firepit Screen",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.5.text",
          "label": "Pits of Fire",
          "item_ref_count": 11,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 11
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit.json",
          "text": "Many useful items can be made in a firepit by heating them. Sticks can be heated, where they will produce two Torches. Note that torches will eventually burn out, and need to be re-lit by using a Firestarter, or using another Torch on them.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.6.text",
          "label": "Pits of Fire",
          "item_ref_count": 11,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 11
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit.json",
          "text": "The fire pit is also a good device for cooking food. All raw meats and doughs can be cooked in a firepit, which will lengthen their shelf life. (More on that here)",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.7.text",
          "label": "Pits of Fire",
          "item_ref_count": 11,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 11
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit.json",
          "text": "The firepit can be extinguished at any time by using a Shovel on it. A firepit can also have other devices added to it to extend its functionality. Using a Wrought Iron Grill will convert the firepit into a Grill, and using a Ceramic Pot will convert the firepit into a Pot. To remove either device, while holding . Be careful not to try to remove a hot grill or pot!",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.8.text",
          "label": "Pits of Fire",
          "item_ref_count": 11,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 11
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit.json",
          "text": "A firepit, with either a grill or pot added.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.9.text",
          "label": "Pits of Fire",
          "item_ref_count": 11,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 11
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/firepit.json",
          "text": "Firepit fuels have different levels of purity. Adding impure fuels to fires makes them more smokey. If the fire burns very impurely, smoke will start to fly very high in the air. The most pure fuels are logs, with pine being the least pure log. Fuels like pinecones and fallen leaves do not hot enough to do much cooking, and are very impure.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.10.text",
          "label": "Pits of Fire",
          "item_ref_count": 11,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 11
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "Clay is an incredibly useful and balanced material which can be used for pottery. It can prove challenging to locate at first. Clay is usually hidden by grass, but it is often found in two locations. In areas with at least 175mm Annual Rainfall, clay can be found in patches all over the place, usually marked by the presence of certain Plants.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.0.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "Clay Indicators",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.1.name",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "Clay, with one of the plants that may indicate its presence.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.1.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "Athyrium Fern, Canna, Goldenrod, Pampas Grass, Perovskia, and Water Canna all indicate the presence of clay nearby. Clay can also be found in smaller deposits close to water sources, such as rivers, lakes, or ponds. Like with rocks, clay can be knapped to form new items. It requires five clay in your hand to knap. Unlike rocks, if you make a mistake, you can simply close the knapping interface, reshape your clay, and try again.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.2.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "The Knapping Interface.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.3.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "The small vessel is one such item. Like all pottery items, it must be fired before it can be used. Firing is a process of heating the item up to a point where the clay will turn into a hard Ceramic material, which requires heating to 1400 °C, or Yellow White. In order to do this in the early game, you will need to use a Pit Kiln.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.4.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "Small Vessel",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.4.title",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "Knapping a Clay Small Vessel.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.5.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "Another useful pottery item is the Jug. It can be used to pick up and drink fluids, such as fresh water. In order to use it, simply the jug on the fluid in the world. Then use the jug in order to drink from it. The jug can hold 100 mB of fluid at a time.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.6.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "Knapping a Clay Jug.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.7.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "Clay is also necessary for making Molds. Molds can have molten metal poured into them, which will eventually solidify into the shape of a mold. The item and potentially the mold can then be retrieved by using on the mold. The most simple type of mold is the ingot mold, to the right.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.8.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "Knapping a Clay Ingot Mold.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.9.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "The mold then needs to be fired, like all clay items, to be usable - likely in a Pit Kiln. Once it is fired, molten metal can be poured in. Once the metal has cooled enough, it can be extracted.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.10.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "The next few pages show several of the knapping patterns for various tools.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.11.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "A Prospector's Pick is an essential tool for locating large quantities of ore.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.12.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "A Pickaxe! The bread and butter tool for mining.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.13.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "A Saw is a tool which is required in order to craft advanced wooden components like a Workbench along with many other devices like Supports.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.14.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "A Scythe is a tool that can harvest plants and leaves in a 3x3x3 area!",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.15.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "A Chisel is a tool used for smoothing blocks as well as creating a large number of decorative blocks.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.16.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "An Axe for all your tree chopping purposes. Note that stone axes are less efficient than metal!",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.17.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "A Hammer is an essential tool to create and work on Anvils.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.18.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "A Knife can be used as a weapon, or as a cutting tool for plant type blocks.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.19.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "A Hoe used for planting and maintaining Crops.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.20.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/getting_started/pottery.json",
          "text": "A Shovel for all your digging purposes.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.21.text",
          "label": "Pottery",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 14,
          "count": 22
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/crucible",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/crucible.json",
          "text": "A Crucible is an advanced device used for the creation of Alloys. It is a more precise method than using a Small Vessel to make alloys. To obtain a crucible, you will first need to obtain some Fire Clay, which is a stronger material than clay. This fire clay can then be knapped to shape it into an Unfired Crucible.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.0.text",
          "label": "Crucible",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 8
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/crucible",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/crucible.json",
          "text": "Knapping an Unfired Crucible.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.1.text",
          "label": "Crucible",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 8
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/crucible",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/crucible.json",
          "text": "After the crucible is knapped, it will need to be fired, like any piece of pottery - a Pit Kiln or Charcoal Forge would do. In order to use the crucible, it needs a source of heat. The crucible can be heated by any heatable block below, usually a Charcoal Forge",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.2.text",
          "label": "Crucible",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 8
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/crucible",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/crucible.json",
          "text": "A crucible heated by a charcoal forge below it.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.3.text",
          "label": "Crucible",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 8
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/crucible",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/crucible.json",
          "text": "Now, you are ready to use the crucible. When you use it, you will see the Crucible Interface, shown to the right. The top region shows the current metal content of the crucible. The first metal shown is what would be produced, if it were to be extracted right now. Other metals shown are the makeup of the current alloy in the crucible.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.4.text",
          "label": "Crucible",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 8
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/crucible",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/crucible.json",
          "text": "Advanced Alloying",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.4.title",
          "label": "Crucible",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 8
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/crucible",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/crucible.json",
          "text": "The Crucible Interface",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.5.text",
          "label": "Crucible",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 8
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/crucible",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/crucible.json",
          "text": "The crucible has nine slots where items can be added to be melted, and their liquefied contents will be directly added to the crucible. Molten metal containers such as Molds can also be placed here and they will be slowly drained into the crucible, allowing for precise control over your alloy's content. Holding while hovering over a draining mold or vessel makes it drain faster. Molds or other fluid containers can also be placed in the output slot, and will be slowly filled with the current content of the crucible.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.6.text",
          "label": "Crucible",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 8
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/crucible",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/crucible.json",
          "text": "The temperature indicator on the left will rise based on external sources of heat, such as a Charcoal Forge below or heat from a Blast Furnace from above. Metal can be extracted from the crucible as long as it is still molten. Finally, the crucible will keep its contents when broken, allowing you to transport the alloy container around if you wish.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.7.text",
          "label": "Crucible",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 8
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay.json",
          "text": "In TerraFirmaCraft, no food will last forever! Food will expire over time, turning rotten. Rotten food will not restore any hunger, and has the potential to give you unhelpful effects such as Hunger or Poison! Fortunately, there are a number of ways to make your food last longer by Preserving it.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.0.text",
          "label": "Preservation",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay.json",
          "text": "When you hover over a piece of food, you will see a tooltip which shows how long the food has until it will rot. It might look something like: Expires on: 5:30 July 5, 1000 (in 5 day(s)) By using various preservation mechanics, that date can be extended, giving you more time before your food rots.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.1.text",
          "label": "Preservation",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay.json",
          "text": "One of the easiest ways to preserve food is to use a Vessel. Large Vessels are a block which can store up to nine items, and when sealed the items inside will gain the Preserved status, which extends their remaining lifetime by 2x. Small Vessels are a item which can store up to four other items, and will also apply the Preserved status to their contents.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.2.text",
          "label": "Preservation",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay.json",
          "text": "A Sealed Large Vessel.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.3.text",
          "label": "Preservation",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay.json",
          "text": "One other way to easily preserve certain types of food is to cook them. Meats will all expire slower when they are cooked than when they are raw. It is also important to use the correct device for cooking. Certain devices that heat very hot, such as a Charcoal Forge or a Crucible are bad for cooking food, which will make them expire faster!",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.4.text",
          "label": "Preservation",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay.json",
          "text": "Instead, a Firepit or a Grill can even provide a buff for using it! For example, cooking mutton (pictured above) in a Firepit will increase its lifetime by 1.33x, and cooking in a Grill will increase its lifetime by 1.66x!",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.5.text",
          "label": "Preservation",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay.json",
          "text": "Salting is a way to make meat last longer. To salt meat, it must be crafted with Salt in a crafting grid. Only raw meat can be salted. Afterwards, cooking or otherwise preserving the meat does not take away the salted property.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.6.text",
          "label": "Preservation",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay.json",
          "text": "One way of getting salt is through grinding Halite, which is a mineral.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.7.text",
          "label": "Preservation",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay.json",
          "text": "Salt Licks",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.8.name",
          "label": "Preservation",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay.json",
          "text": "Salt can be found naturally in forests. It can be placed and picked back up.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.8.text",
          "label": "Preservation",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay.json",
          "text": "Vinegar Preservation is a way of making fruits, veggies, and meat last longer. Vinegar is made in a Barrel, by sealing a fruit with 250mB of Alcohol. To preserve food in vinegar it must first be Pickled in Brine. Brine is made in a barrel with 1 part Vinegar and 9 parts Salt Water.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.9.text",
          "label": "Preservation",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay.json",
          "text": "Once food is pickled, it can be sealed in a Barrel of Vinegar. If there is 125mB of Vinegar per pickled food item, the food will last longer.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.10.text",
          "label": "Preservation",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/decay.json",
          "text": "Food should be stored in either sealed large vessels or in Small Vessels. Food that is left sitting in chests or other devices can attract Rats. Rats are able to open containers and eat the food out of them, but will despawn if they can't find something for a few minutes. You will be alerted to a rat's presence by the message 'This container has a foul smell'. It is important to note that unsealing and resealing a large vessel before you leave the screen will never attract pests.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.11.text",
          "label": "Preservation",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fire_clay",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fire_clay.json",
          "text": "Fire Clay",
          "key": "guide-page:name",
          "label": "Fire Clay",
          "item_ref_count": 6,
          "recipe_ref_count": 5,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fire_clay",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fire_clay.json",
          "text": "The list of uses of fire clay is small, but all of them are important. Fire clay is a stronger variant of clay that has better heat resistance. It is used to make things that have to get very hot!",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.0.text",
          "label": "Fire Clay",
          "item_ref_count": 6,
          "recipe_ref_count": 5,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fire_clay",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fire_clay.json",
          "text": "Fire clay is made from graphite powder, crushed in a quern, as well as kaolinite powder",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.1.text",
          "label": "Fire Clay",
          "item_ref_count": 6,
          "recipe_ref_count": 5,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fire_clay",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fire_clay.json",
          "text": "Kaolinite powder is made by heating Kaolin Clay. However, the process is not perfect, and only 20% of clay will form powder!",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.2.text",
          "label": "Fire Clay",
          "item_ref_count": 6,
          "recipe_ref_count": 5,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fire_clay",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fire_clay.json",
          "text": "The Crucible in its unfired state is made from fire clay.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.3.text",
          "label": "Fire Clay",
          "item_ref_count": 6,
          "recipe_ref_count": 5,
          "count": 6
        }
      ],
      "aliases": []
    },

    {
      "id": "tfc:anvil",
      "label": "Anvil",
      "origin": "namespace_generated",
      "confidence": 0.85,
      "support": 574,
      "evidence": [
        {

        }
      ],
      "semantic_evidence": [
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/armor",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/armor.json",
          "text": "Armor provides protection against attacks from predators and monsters. The quality of armor scales with the tier of the Metal, with Leather being the weakest and Colored Steels being the strongest.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.0.text",
          "label": "Armor",
          "item_ref_count": 6,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/armor",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/armor.json",
          "text": "Leather armor is Knapped from Leather. It does not last long, but provides some decent protection if you have a full suit.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.1.text",
          "label": "Armor",
          "item_ref_count": 6,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/armor",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/armor.json",
          "text": "Metal Armor requires multiple processing steps in an Anvil. First, an unfinished armor piece must be smithed. These require a Double Sheet of the metal, except for boots which require a single sheet.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.2.text",
          "label": "Armor",
          "item_ref_count": 6,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/armor",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/armor.json",
          "text": "Next, a Sheet must be Welded to the armor piece to finish it. Chestplates require a Double Sheet to be finished.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.3.text",
          "label": "Armor",
          "item_ref_count": 6,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/armor",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/armor.json",
          "text": "Armor that is of the same tier but different metals may be subtly different. These are expressed in durability, as well as Damage Resistances. In order of increasing durability, the bronzes are ranked Bismuth Bronze, regular Bronze, and then Black Bronze. For colored steels, Red Steel lasts longer than Blue Steel.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.4.text",
          "label": "Armor",
          "item_ref_count": 6,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/armor",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/armor.json",
          "text": "Steel armor also provides benefits such as Toughness and Knockback Resistance. Regular Steel has 1 toughness, Black Steel has 2 toughness, and the Colored Steels have 3 toughness. Black Steel has 5% knockback resistance, whereas the Colored Steels have 10%.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.5.text",
          "label": "Armor",
          "item_ref_count": 6,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery.json",
          "text": "The Bloomery is a device used to smelt Iron Ore into Iron Blooms which can be worked into Wrought Iron. Some common iron ores are Hematite, Limonite, and Magnetite. These ores melt into Cast Iron rather than Wrought Iron. All iron-bearing items melt into Cast Iron. To turn them into usable iron, the bloomery is needed. Any iron item can be used in the bloomery, including iron tools and cast iron ingots!",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.0.text",
          "label": "Bloomery",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 10
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery.json",
          "text": "The bloomery is made from 8 Bronze Double Plates.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.1.text",
          "label": "Bloomery",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 10
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery.json",
          "text": "A Bloomery",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.2.name",
          "label": "Bloomery",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 10
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery.json",
          "text": "A minimum size bloomery. The bloomery block will open and close with .",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.2.text",
          "label": "Bloomery",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 10
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery.json",
          "text": "The bloomery can contain up to a maximum of 48 Inputs, with 16 items per layer of the chimney. To add layers to the chimney, stack up two more layers of stone blocks. To add items to the bloomery, climb up to the top and throw items inside. A tower of grey ore should form. You can use both Charcoal and Coal as fuel for your bloomery.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.3.text",
          "label": "Bloomery",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 10
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery.json",
          "text": "The bloomery consumes 1 item of Fuel and 144 mB of Cast Iron to produce one Bloom.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.4.text",
          "label": "Bloomery",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 10
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery.json",
          "text": "If you don't want to do the math, we recommend 25 metal ore dusts and 22 fuel items. After filling the bloomery with a combination of Fuel and Ore, light the bloomery doors, and wait 15 hours for the bloomery to smelt. When the bloomery shuts off, it leaves behind a Bloom block. This contains Raw Iron Blooms which can be obtained by mining the Bloom repeatedly with a pickaxe.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.5.text",
          "label": "Bloomery",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 10
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery.json",
          "text": "The Bloom Block",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.6.name",
          "label": "Bloomery",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 10
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery.json",
          "text": "A large Bloom.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.6.text",
          "label": "Bloomery",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 10
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery.json",
          "text": "The Raw Iron Bloom must be worked in a anvil to make Refined Iron Bloom.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.7.text",
          "label": "Bloomery",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 10
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery.json",
          "text": "The Refined Iron Bloom must be worked in a anvil to make Wrought Iron Ingots.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.8.text",
          "label": "Bloomery",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 10
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery.json",
          "text": "- If the bloomery finds itself with more items contained than it can handle based on its chimney, it will try to spit them out the front. - To retrieve your items from a bloomery that is not lit, do not break the molten block tower. Break the bloomery block. - Blooms will only melt into cast iron, not wrought iron. They must be worked!",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.9.text",
          "label": "Bloomery",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 3,
          "count": 10
        },
        {

          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bloomery",

          "count": 10
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fishing",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fishing.json",
          "text": "Fishing is a way of hunting the fish that swim around in rivers, lakes, and oceans. Fishing rods must be baited and cast. Fish attempt to eat the bait, and sometimes succeed. Reeling in a fish takes work, and becomes easier with higher level hooks.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.0.text",
          "label": "Fishing",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fishing",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fishing.json",
          "text": "First, you have to forge a fishing hook in an Anvil.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.1.text",
          "label": "Fishing",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fishing",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fishing.json",
          "text": "Fishing Rod",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.2.title",
          "label": "Fishing",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fishing",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fishing.json",
          "text": "The fishing rod is crafted with a fishing hook.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.2.text",
          "label": "Fishing",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fishing",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fishing.json",
          "text": "Fishing rods are not useful without bait. Bait can be added to rods in a crafting table. To catch normal fish, you need Seeds or Shellfish. To catch larger fish, such as Dolphins and Orcas, you need cod, salmon, tropical fish, or bluegills.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.3.text",
          "label": "Fishing",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fishing",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fishing.json",
          "text": "To release the bobber, . Wait for a fish to spot the hook and bite it. Then to pull it in. As you do that, the meter on your hotbar will fill up. Pull too quickly, and the fish will get away with the bait. Each time you fish, the fish has a chance of eating the bait. To catch the fish, pull it up on land and kill it with a tool. You can hold the fishing rod in your off hand to make this easier.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.4.text",
          "label": "Fishing",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fishing",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/fishing.json",
          "text": "The fishing bar replaces the experience bar when active.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.5.text",
          "label": "Fishing",
          "item_ref_count": 7,
          "recipe_ref_count": 2,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking.json",
          "text": "Glassworking is the process of turning sand into glass. To start, you must create a Glass Batch, of which there are four types: 1. Silica, from white sand. 2. Hematitic, from yellow, red, or pink sand. 3. Olivine, from green or brown sand. 4. Volcanic, from black sand.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.0.text",
          "label": "Glassworking",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 8,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking.json",
          "text": "Silica Glass Batch",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.1.title",
          "label": "Glassworking",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 8,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking.json",
          "text": "Glass batches can then be crafted using one of the aforementioned colors of sand, plus Lime and a type of Potash.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.1.text",
          "label": "Glassworking",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 8,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking.json",
          "text": "Lime is one of the ingredients required to make glass batches. It is a powder obtained by heating Flux.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.2.text",
          "label": "Glassworking",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 8,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking.json",
          "text": "A type of Potash or equivalent is also required for glass batches. Soda Ash can be used, which is a powder made from heating Dried Seaweed or Kelp. Saltpeter can be used as well.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.3.text",
          "label": "Glassworking",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 8,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking.json",
          "text": "Glassworking is done by starting with a glass batch, and then completing a series of steps. These steps may require specific tools: - A Blowpipe, to Blow and Stretch - A Paddle, to Flatten - Jacks, to Pinch - A Gem Saw, to Saw",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.4.text",
          "label": "Glassworking",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 8,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking.json",
          "text": "Tools of the Trade",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.4.title",
          "label": "Glassworking",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 8,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking.json",
          "text": "The most important tool is the Blowpipe. It can be knapped from clay, and then fired into a Ceramic Blowpipe.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.5.text",
          "label": "Glassworking",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 8,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking.json",
          "text": "Ceramic blowpipes are brittle, and have a chance to to break when used. A more sturdy blowpipe can be worked from a Brass Rod on an anvil.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.6.text",
          "label": "Glassworking",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 8,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking.json",
          "text": "The Flatten operation can be done with a Paddle, which is crafted from wood.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.7.text",
          "label": "Glassworking",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 8,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking.json",
          "text": "The Pinch operation can be done with Jacks, made from welding two brass rods together.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.8.text",
          "label": "Glassworking",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 8,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking.json",
          "text": "The Saw operation can be done with a Gem Saw. The gem saw is also used to break both Glass Blocks and Glass Panes and obtain them.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.9.text",
          "label": "Glassworking",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 8,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking.json",
          "text": "First, glass on the blowpipe must be heated to Faint Red. Then, hold the blowpipe in your offhand and hold to perform each step. Use to pick up a hot blowpipe into your offhand. Blow Use the Blowpipe while facing straight ahead. Stretch Use the Blowpipe while facing straight down.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.10.text",
          "label": "Glassworking",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 8,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking.json",
          "text": "How to Glass",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.10.title",
          "label": "Glassworking",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 8,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking.json",
          "text": "Flatten Use the Blowpipe while holding a Paddle in your main hand. Pinch Use the Blowpipe while holding Jacks in your main hand. Saw Use the Blowpipe while holding a Gem Saw in your main hand. Roll Use the Blowpipe with a Wool Cloth in your main hand.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.11.text",
          "label": "Glassworking",
          "item_ref_count": 9,
          "recipe_ref_count": 8,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking.json",
          "text": "Glassworking is the process of turning sand into glass. To start, you must create a Glass Batch, of which there are four types: 1. Silica, from white sand. 2. Hematitic, from yellow, red, or pink sand. 3. Olivine, from green or brown sand. 4. Volcanic, from black sand.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.0.text",
          "label": "Glassworking",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 8,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking.json",
          "text": "Glass batches can then be crafted using one of the aforementioned colors of sand, plus Lime and a type of Potash.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.1.text",
          "label": "Glassworking",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 8,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/glassworking.json",
          "text": "Lime is one of the ingredients required to make glass batches. It is a powder obtained by heating Flux.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.2.text",
          "label": "Glassworking",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 8,
          "count": 12
        },
        {

          "text": "A type of Potash or equivalent is also required for glass batches. Soda Ash can be used, which is a powder made from heating Dried Seaweed or Kelp. Saltpeter can be used as well.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.3.text",
          "label": "Glassworking",

    {
      "id": "tfc:quern",
      "label": "Quern Recipe",

      "support": 474,
      "evidence": [
        {

        }
      ],
      "semantic_evidence": [
        {
          "kind": "recipe_type",
          "id": "tfc:quern",
          "source": "file:minecraft/lang-overlays",
          "text": "Quern Recipe",
          "key": "recipe-category-lang:tfc.jei.quern",
          "label": "Quern Recipe",
          "recipe_type": "tfc:quern",
          "count": 1
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bread",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bread.json",
          "text": "Bread is the processed form of the various grain crops, such as Barley. Breaking a grain crop drops a raw, unprocessed grain item, which is not useful on its own. It must be processed into Bread, which can then be eaten or used in Sandwiches.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.0.text",
          "label": "Bread",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 4,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bread",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bread.json",
          "text": "First, cut the straw off of the food with a Knife.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.1.text",
          "label": "Bread",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 4,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bread",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bread.json",
          "text": "Grains are the longest-lasting stage of the process, decaying much slower than most foods. On its own, a fresh piece of grain lasts 10 months and 7 days. In a small vessel, it lasts 1 year, 9 months, and 7 days.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.2.text",
          "label": "Bread",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 4,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bread",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bread.json",
          "text": "Grain must then be ground in a Quern to make flour.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.3.text",
          "label": "Bread",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 4,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bread",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bread.json",
          "text": "Dough is crafted by adding a bucket of Fresh Water to flour.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.4.text",
          "label": "Bread",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 4,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bread",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/bread.json",
          "text": "Dough is then able to be heated to make bread. At this point it can also be used in Sandwiches.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.5.text",
          "label": "Bread",
          "item_ref_count": 8,
          "recipe_ref_count": 4,
          "count": 6
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/flux",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/flux.json",
          "text": "Flux is a powder which is required for Welding and also used as a catalyst in a Blast Furnace. Flux can be obtained by grinding specific items in a Quern. Flux can be obtained in a number of ways, one of which is from its native ore, Borax.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.0.text",
          "label": "Flux",
          "item_ref_count": 4,
          "recipe_ref_count": 1,
          "count": 2
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/flux",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/flux.json",
          "text": "Some rocks - Limestone, Dolomite, Chalk, or Marble - can also be used as flux, after being ground in a Quern. Other items, including Scutes, Clams, Mollusks, and the edible remains of Shellfish can also be used to create flux.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.1.text",
          "label": "Flux",
          "item_ref_count": 4,
          "recipe_ref_count": 1,
          "count": 2
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/quern",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/quern.json",
          "text": "The Quern is a device for grinding items. It can crush raw ores for processing, as well as make powders, dyes, and some other items. It is assembled from a Base and Handstone.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.0.text",
          "label": "Quern",
          "item_ref_count": 12,
          "recipe_ref_count": 5,
          "count": 11
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/quern",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/quern.json",
          "text": "The base of the quern can be crafted with three smooth stone and three of any other Stone blocks. Stone blocks can be acquired via extraction, and smooth blocks with the chisel.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.1.text",
          "label": "Quern",
          "item_ref_count": 12,
          "recipe_ref_count": 5,
          "count": 11
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/quern",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/quern.json",
          "text": "The quern needs a Handstone to operate.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.2.text",
          "label": "Quern",
          "item_ref_count": 12,
          "recipe_ref_count": 5,
          "count": 11
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/quern",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/quern.json",
          "text": "Point at the top of the quern block and to place the handstone.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.3.text",
          "label": "Quern",
          "item_ref_count": 12,
          "recipe_ref_count": 5,
          "count": 11
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/quern",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/quern.json",
          "text": "Use on the top of the handstone to add items.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.4.text",
          "label": "Quern",
          "item_ref_count": 12,
          "recipe_ref_count": 5,
          "count": 11
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/quern",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/quern.json",
          "text": "Use the handle to spin the handstone.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.5.text",
          "label": "Quern",
          "item_ref_count": 12,
          "recipe_ref_count": 5,
          "count": 11
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/quern",
          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/quern.json",
          "text": "The output should appear on the base of the quern. anywhere on the base to retrieve it.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.6.text",
          "label": "Quern",
          "item_ref_count": 12,
          "recipe_ref_count": 5,
          "count": 11
        },
        {

          "source": "file:minecraft/kubejs/assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/quern.json",
          "text": "Crops can be processed with a knife or quern to acquire Grain, which can further be ground into Flour.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.10.text",
          "label": "Quern",
          "item_ref_count": 12,
          "recipe_ref_count": 5,
          "count": 11
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",
          "id": "tfc:field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/quern",
          "source": "jar:TerraFirmaCraft-Forge-1.20.1-3.2.21.jar!assets/tfc/patchouli_books/field_guide/en_us/entries/mechanics/quern.json",
          "text": "The Quern is a device for grinding items. It can make powders, dyes, and some other items. It is assembled from a Base and Handstone. The Quern can also be connected to a Mechanical Power network.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.0.text",
          "label": "Quern",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 7,
          "count": 12
        },
        {

          "text": "The base of the quern can be crafted with three smooth stone and three of any other Stone blocks.",
          "key": "guide-page:pages.1.text",
          "label": "Quern",
          "item_ref_count": 10,
          "recipe_ref_count": 7,
          "count": 12
        },
        {
          "kind": "guide_page",

          "text": "The quern needs a Handstone to operate.",

          "label": "Quern",

          "recipe_ref_count": 7,
          "count": 12
        },
        {

          "count": 12
